result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly identify the roughly 1.7:1 body-text contrast and the clustered mid-tone olive palette, and their spot-checked contrast figures are accurate. A ranks the problems explicitly by impact and gives concrete hex values for every role, including a clearly alarming error red. B explains why the palette looks muddy a little better, but it leaves the secondary and link colors vague and keeps the error color deliberately 'not alarming', which undercuts the job an error color has to do. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers quote accurate contrast figures: about 1.7:1 for body text on the background, and correct link, error and button ratios. Both also propose warm, sensible replacements built on a cream background, dark warm text and a teal primary. B is slightly better because it ranks the problems by impact with body text first, gives concrete values for every role including links and secondary buttons, and points out that the error colour reads as brand-brown rather than an alert. A lists low contrast third, though it does later call body text the worst problem.
